_comment: Config-driven agent/model registry for the GEAK standalone runtime. Two orthogonal axes: 'agents' (how to drive a code-agent CLI, model-independent) and 'models' (an endpoint, CLI-independent). A 'profile' pins one (agent, model) combo. See SETUP.md R1-R7 for the fields that must be confirmed per CLI with `<cli> --help` at bring-up. Flags below are best-effort defaults; override any without editing code via env (GEAK_<CLI>_* / GEAK_QWEN_EXTRA_ARGS) or a backends/<name>.mjs escape hatch. An agent's 'credential_env' lists every env var that means 'this CLI's provider side is configured' (its provider_autoselect trigger_env names count too). Auto-selection reads it as an EXCLUSION: a key only selects its own agent when no OTHER agent's side is configured, so exporting a gateway key next to an existing Claude setup falls back to default_profile instead of silently moving the run onto codex. Same rule as hyperloom's is_openai_only()/is_anthropic_only() in common/llm_config.py.

qwen.note: non-interactive auth needs ~/.qwen/settings.json {security.auth.selectedType:'openai'}; OpenAI-compatible via OPENAI_API_KEY/OPENAI_BASE_URL, which is the ONLY way to give it an endpoint — it sends the key as a Bearer and cannot attach a custom auth header, so a gateway needing one (like AMD's Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key) is out of reach. Last verified 2026-07-31 against the now-decommissioned SaFE gateway; re-confirm against whatever endpoint you point it at.

codex.note: Rust bin: wire_api=responses. Provider is AUTO-CONFIGURED via `-c model_providers.geak_auto.*` overrides; codex needs no config.toml and no CODEX_HOME. Resolution: (1) explicit OPENAI_BASE_URL (or the selected model's base_url) is used directly; (2) else key-driven auto-SELECT walks provider_autoselect and picks the first provider whose trigger_env is set — AMDKEY->AMD (adds Ocp-Apim header), OPENAI_API_KEY->OpenAI official. Those same trigger_env names also SELECT this agent when nothing was named explicitly (see deriveAgentFromEnv in config.mjs), so configuring a key is by itself enough to run on codex. Each entry also carries default_model — the id used when GEAK_CODEX_MODEL is unset; it lives in the SAME entry as base_url because a model id is only valid on its own endpoint. The AMD gateway (which replaces the decommissioned SaFE one) authenticates on Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key ALONE — a Bearer-only request is a 401, the header alone is a 200 on both /responses and /chat/completions (measured 2026-09-09, gpt-5.6-sol); env_key is emitted anyway because codex requires one and the extra Bearer is harmless. Its gpt models work on both wire protocols; its Claude models mostly do not answer for this subscription (500/504), which is why no claude model is pinned. Disable with GEAK_CODEX_AUTOCONFIG=0 (provider) / GEAK_AGENT_AUTO=0 (selection); GEAK_CODEX_EXTRA_ARGS with model_provider= wins. SSL_CERT_FILE still needed for intranet-gateway CAs (not public OpenAI).

kimi.note: official kimi-cli (PyPI, install via uv --python 3.13). OpenAI-compatible via ~/.kimi/config.toml (type=openai_legacy, default_model). --quiet=print+final-only, --afk=unattended auto-approve. Needs SSL_CERT_FILE for gateway CA. prompt is the value of -p (last arg); model via config default_model (generic path omits -m to keep -p<prompt> adjacent).

cursor.note: AgentKernelArena-style cursor-agent CLI (--force --print). Auth via cursor-agent's own login / CURSOR_API_KEY in env; runs on Cursor cloud (NOT SaFE gateway); no base_url. Model = Cursor-side id (e.g. sonnet-4-thinking). Verify --output-format/model against `cursor-agent --help` at bring-up; stream-json parsing may be needed if text mode is noisy.

_models_comment: Pinned endpoints, CLI-independent. base_url is applied to the agent's base_url_env; keys stay in env (never in this file). The old SaFE gateway (global.primus-safe.amd.com) is DECOMMISSIONED — its entries were dropped rather than repointed. The AMD gateway that replaces it (llm-api.amd.com/Unified, reached via AMDKEY in codex's provider_autoselect) authenticates on the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header, which only the codex path can send; qwen/kimi have no way to attach it, so no gateway-backed model is listed for them. Point them at an endpoint yourself via OPENAI_BASE_URL if needed.

openai_official.note: Official OpenAI (api.openai.com). Standard Bearer auth via OPENAI_API_KEY (sk-...); public CA, no shim, no APIM header. `id` is a REQUIRED placeholder — set GEAK_CODEX_MODEL to a real OpenAI model your account serves over the Responses API (the provider_autoselect default is gpt-5.6-sol; entitlement is per-account, so override when yours differs). Use openai_gpt56 instead if you just want plain gpt-5.6.

openai_gpt56.note: Official OpenAI, plain gpt-5.6 — the suffixless id, which exists ONLY here: the AMD gateway serves gpt-5.6-sol/-terra/-luna and 404s plain gpt-5.6, so the two sets are not interchangeable. Bearer auth via OPENAI_API_KEY, public CA, no shim, no APIM header. Pin it (`--profile codex-gpt56`) to reach the official model even while a gateway key is also exported — a pinned model brings its own base_url and outranks provider_autoselect. Not reachable from this repo for a live check (no OPENAI_API_KEY), so the shape is taken from hyperloom, which runs this exact combination: kernelforge pins DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL = 'gpt-5.6' (agent_backends/codex.py) and its provider registry declares codex default_model 'gpt-5.6', while resolve_openai_gateway (kernelforge/llm/gateway.py) attaches base_url + env_key OPENAI_API_KEY and NO custom headers unless OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS is set explicitly. Availability is still per-account entitlement; on a 404/400 fall back to openai_official + GEAK_CODEX_MODEL.
